obligations.timing: Payment by the 15th of the following month; SPT Masa within 20 days after the period ends; a Saturday, Sunday, public holiday or national cuti bersama moves either to the next working day
obligations.owner: Finance / billing code, payment and SPT Masa receipt
obligations.authority: PMK 81/2024 art.94(2) (payment; https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/306614/pmk-no-81-tahun-2024); UU KUP art.3(3)(a) (SPT Masa 20 days); PER-11/PJ/2025 (https://jdih.kemenkeu.go.id/dok/per-11pj2025); late filing Rp100,000 per SPT Masa (UU KUP art.7(1)), late payment interest (art.9(2a))

obligations.description: Issue Form BPA1 (formerly 1721-A1) to each permanent employee for the year, or for the part year to departure
obligations.trigger: The last tax period: December, or the month a permanent employee stops working
obligations.timing: Within one month after the last tax period ends
obligations.owner: Finance / BPA1 delivered to the employee
obligations.authority: PER-11/PJ/2025 art.7(2) (https://jdih.kemenkeu.go.id/dok/per-11pj2025); PMK 168/2023 (the annual reckoning the form reports)

obligations.description: Obtain each employee's NIK/NPWP and PTKP status (marital status, dependants, a married woman's statement that her husband has no income)
obligations.trigger: Hire, and the start of each calendar year
obligations.timing: PTKP is fixed on the employee's condition at the start of the calendar year (PMK 168/2023 art.9)
obligations.authority: PMK 168/2023 art.9 (https://pajak.go.id/sites/default/files/2024-02/PMK%20168%20Tahun%202023%20Tentang%20PPh%20Pasal%2021%20TER.pdf); UU PPh art.21(5a) (20% higher withholding without NPWP; DJP applies none where a valid NIK is given)

obligations.description: Keep the books, records and documents on which withholding is based
obligations.trigger: Each record
obligations.timing: 10 years in Indonesia

obligations.description: Pay wages in rupiah, in full, at the agreed time, at intervals of not more than one month
obligations.trigger: Each pay date
obligations.timing: The agreed date; the pay interval may not exceed 1 month (art.55(4)). Late wages: 5% per day from the 4th to the 8th day, then +1% per day capped at 50% in a month, then bank interest after a month (art.61)

obligations.description: Give each worker a proof of wage payment with the wage details
obligations.trigger: Each wage payment
obligations.timing: "pada saat Upah dibayarkan" — at the time the wage is paid

obligations.description: Deduct from wages only for fines, damages, advances, rent, debts or overpayment on the required basis, and never more than half of each payment
obligations.trigger: Each deduction other than tax and social security
obligations.timing: Each payment: the total of deductions at most 50% of the wage paid (art.65); rent and debts need written agreement, third-party deductions a revocable power of attorney (arts.63–64)

obligations.description: Pay no worker below the applicable provincial or city/regency minimum wage; basic wage at least 75% of basic plus fixed allowances
obligations.trigger: Each new minimum-wage decree (in force 1 January) and each wage change
obligations.timing: From the decree's commencement
obligations.authority: PP 36/2021 arts.7, 23(3), 25 as amended by PP 51/2023 (https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/161909/pp-no-36-tahun-2021); the governor's UMP/UMK decree for the year

obligations.description: Draw up and apply a wage structure and scale and notify each worker of the grade that applies to them
obligations.trigger: Standing duty; each change
obligations.timing: Standing; each worker notified individually

obligations.description: Pay the religious holiday allowance (THR) before the worker's religious holiday
obligations.trigger: Each religious holiday of the worker (Idulfitri, Christmas, Nyepi, Waisak, Imlek)
obligations.timing: "paling lambat 7 (tujuh) hari sebelum Hari Raya Keagamaan" (art.5(4)); a late payment carries a 5% fine of the THR due (art.10), without discharging the THR

obligations.description: Record each fixed-term employment agreement (PKWT) with the Ministry of Manpower
obligations.trigger: Signing of a PKWT or its extension
obligations.timing: Online within 3 working days of signing; in writing at the city/regency manpower office within 7 working days where the online service is unavailable

obligations.description: Overtime by written or digital order and the worker's consent, a signed list and a record of names and hours; rest and food for long overtime; the daily and weekly caps
obligations.trigger: Overtime is requested or worked
obligations.timing: Before the overtime (order and consent); a list of each worker's overtime hours kept; at most 4 hours a day and 18 a week outside rest days and public holidays; 1,400 kcal of food and drink for 4 hours or more, not payable in cash

obligations.description: Termination by written notice stating the reason, bipartite negotiation on a rejection, and payment of the compensation for the cause
obligations.trigger: Each termination initiated by the employer, and each legally defined cause
obligations.timing: Notice at least 14 working days before termination, 7 during probation (art.37(3)–(4)); the worker may reject in writing within 7 working days, then bipartite negotiation and industrial-relations settlement (art.39)
obligations.owner: HR / notices, consultation, cause and settlement evidence

obligations.description: Report an unopposed termination to the manpower ministry or provincial/regency manpower office
obligations.trigger: The worker received the notice and did not reject it
obligations.timing: After the notice period, on termination

obligations.description: Company employment report (Wajib Lapor Ketenagakerjaan di Perusahaan) through the online WLKP service
obligations.trigger: Establishing, reopening, moving or closing the company; each year
obligations.timing: Within 30 days after or before establishing, reopening or moving (art.6); every year thereafter (art.8)
obligations.authority: UU 7/1981 arts.6, 8 (https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/47039/uu-no-7-tahun-1981); Permenaker 18/2017 as amended by Permenaker 4/2019

obligations.description: Company regulations (Peraturan Perusahaan) for an employer of ten or more workers, ratified by the ministry or manpower office, unless a collective agreement applies
obligations.trigger: Ten or more workers
obligations.timing: In force once ratified; valid at most 2 years and then renewed

obligations.description: Approved foreign-worker employment plan (RPTKA) and the foreign-worker compensation fund (DKPTKA) for each foreign worker
obligations.trigger: Each foreign worker employed
obligations.timing: DKPTKA paid on the billing code before the RPTKA is approved, for the period the worker works in Indonesia (art.23(2)–(5))
obligations.owner: HR / RPTKA approval and DKPTKA receipt

obligations.description: Process worker personal data only on a lawful basis (explicit valid consent, performance of the employment contract, a legal obligation such as BPJS and PPh 21 reporting, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interest); where processing rests on consent, inform the worker of the legality, purpose, data types, retention period, processing period and their rights, and tell them before any change.
obligations.trigger: Collection or processing of an applicant's or worker's personal data
obligations.timing: Before processing; before any change to the information given
obligations.owner: HR / privacy notice and consent record
obligations.authority: UU 27/2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi arts.20–21 (https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/229798/uu-no-27-tahun-2022); fully applicable from 17 October 2024 (art.74: two years from promulgation on 17 October 2022)

obligations.description: Protect and secure the personal data processed (technical and operational measures, security level set by the data's nature and risk), keep it confidential, supervise every party processing under the controller's control (a payroll vendor), and prevent unlawful processing and access.
obligations.trigger: Holding or processing worker personal data
obligations.timing: Continuous

obligations.description: Carry out a personal data protection impact assessment where processing is high-risk (automated decisions with legal or significant effect, specific data such as health, biometric or financial data, large-scale processing, systematic evaluation, scoring or monitoring, data matching, new technology).
obligations.trigger: Introduction of high-risk processing (for example biometric attendance or large-scale payroll processing of health data)
obligations.timing: Before the high-risk processing begins

obligations.description: Delete personal data no longer needed for its purpose, on withdrawal of consent or request, or when unlawfully obtained; destroy it when its retention period under the archive schedule ends or on request; notify the worker of the deletion or destruction.
obligations.trigger: End of the purpose or retention period, withdrawal of consent, or a data-subject request
obligations.timing: When the condition arises, subject to other statutory retention periods (tax and BPJS records)
obligations.owner: HR / retention schedule and destruction record

obligations.description: On a failure of personal data protection, give written notice to the affected data subjects and to the PDP agency stating the data exposed, when and how it was exposed, and the handling and recovery measures; in certain cases also notify the public.
obligations.trigger: A failure of personal data protection (breach) affecting worker personal data
obligations.timing: No later than 3 × 24 hours

obligations.description: Appoint an officer performing the personal data protection function (internal or external) where processing serves a public service, where core activities require regular and systematic large-scale monitoring, or where core activities are large-scale processing of specific data or criminal-record data.
obligations.trigger: The employer meets an art.53(1) criterion
obligations.timing: Before or when the criterion is met; continuous
